SUPERSEDED - benign phase aborted after run 1 and re-run in full. The T1547.001 mirror's Startup-folder shortcut failed with 'Missing )' in method call'. Cause: Invoke-ViaPowerShell passed the command as a bare array element to Start-Process, which does not re-quote elements, and Windows command-line parsing then CONSUMED the double quotes around a path containing a space ('Start Menu'). The child PowerShell received an unquoted, space-split path. The same quote-stripping had been happening silently in EVERY earlier mirror (T1082, T1033, T1016, T1136.001) and never mattered, because -Path HKCU:\Software\... parses identically with or without quotes. A latent bug that only manifests when an argument contains a space. Retained rather than deleted: the run produced 1 real window of partial benign telemetry (2 of 4 mechanisms succeeded), and silently dropping it would hide that the benign class was briefly incomplete. Invoke-ViaPowerShell now escapes inner quotes and wraps the command in one quoted argument. -EncodedCommand was rejected as the fix: it is immune to quoting but would make every benign mirror emit a base64 command line, tripping rule 92057 and turning encoding into a benign-class marker - a class-correlated confound worse than the bug. [Note text restored 2026-08-08 after a merge-script defect blanked the notes column.]

T1547.001 BASELINE benign, RE-RUN. Replaces the 07:07-07:20 baseline benign windows, which are now superseded. Reason: the benign mirror gained a FIFTH command after the first baseline benign phase had already run. WHY THE FIFTH COMMAND WAS NEEDED: rule 100290 keys on the VALUE CONTENT of a Run entry - interpreters, encoded commands, temp paths, URLs - and ART's atomic 3 payload is powershell.exe with an inline download cradle, while all four original mirror commands registered a plain .exe path. 100290 would therefore have come out attack-only for a reason that is not a real discriminator: an adversary can point a Run key at a plain .exe, and legitimate management software registers interpreters at logon. This is the FIFTH time a mirror narrower than the attack set would have manufactured a fake discriminator (100241, 100251, 100271, 100282) but the FIRST where the gap is the value's CONTENT rather than the MECHANISM. Mechanism gaps are visible when listing the atomics; content gaps only surface when reading your own rule's regex against your own mirror's data. RE-RUN RATHER THAN CAVEATED: 13 minutes to remove a confound from the technique whose headline finding IS class overlap. Both phases now share one identical 5-command mirror, so baseline vs custom differs only by the ruleset.

T1547.001 CUSTOM phase. Rules 100290, 100291, 100292, 100294 deployed and smoke-tested first. ⚠️ WAZUH EVALUATES SIBLING CHILD RULES BY DESCENDING LEVEL, NOT BY LOAD ORDER OR ID - measured in the smoke test, not assumed, and it contradicted what I had written in the rule comments. Evidence: 100291 (L8) displaced 92302 (L6) on a reg.exe Run-key write; 100294 (L10) displaced 92201 (L9) on a powershell-created Startup .lnk; 100290 (L12) displaced 100291 (L8) on an interpreter payload. CONSEQUENCE FOR READING THESE COUNTS: 92302 is now DISPLACED, so custom-phase T1547.001 alerts must be split into RELABELLED (what 92302 already caught: 4 attack / 5 benign in baseline) and NEWLY VISIBLE (everything 92300 matched but never emitted). Reporting the total as new detection would overstate the contribution - same treatment T1136.001 needed. LEVELS WERE NOT LOWERED TO AVOID THE DISPLACEMENT. Setting 100291 to level 5 would have handed the reg.exe case back to the vendor rule, but choosing a severity to manipulate evaluation order rather than to express how serious the behaviour is would be bad detection engineering. 100293 REMOVED AS UNREACHABLE before this phase ran: it chained from 92201 (L9), but 100294 (L10) is 92201's sibling under 92200 and always wins for Startup-folder paths, so 92201 never matched and its child could never fire. ID retired, not reused. This also CORRECTED the baseline analysis - 92201 was not the rule misattributing the Startup .lnk to T1105; 92200 (L6) was. VENDOR PRECISION DEFECT FOUND IN PASSING: rule 92041 (L10, 'Value added to registry key has Base64-like pattern', mapped to T1027 Obfuscated Files) fired on the plain path C:\ProgramData\Smoke\viareg.exe. It asserts obfuscation where there is none, which is why it showed 4 attack / 5 benign in the baseline. ⚠️ attack-r1 window is 81s against ~7s for runs 2-5 - first-invocation ART module load, not a failure, but it captures more ambient telemetry than its siblings. Check per-window variance before quoting per-window counts.

T1112 CUSTOM phase - custom rules deployed, SENSOR UNCHANGED. This phase isolates the RULE fix. Rules 100263/100264 repair 92041, the only default rule that fires and claims T1112. 92041 lives in 0800-sysmon_id_1.xml - it is a PROCESS CREATION rule that never reads the registry - and its regex (?i)add.+/d\s+(")?(?:[A-Za-z\d+/]{4})*(?:[A-Za-z\d+/]{3}=|[A-Za-z\d+/]{2}==)? has every group after /d quantified * or ?, so zero repetitions satisfy it. Verified: it matches any 'reg add ... /d <anything>', including 'add x /d ' with nothing following. It fired 30 attack / 15 benign in baseline - exactly one per reg add issued (6 per attack run, 3 per benign run) - while asserting T1027 Obfuscated Files, false in all 45 cases. 100263 restores a real base64 test (>=16 chars) and keeps T1027 where it is true; 100264 catches the rest and drops the false T1027, leaving T1112. EXPECT 100263 TO FIRE ZERO TIMES: none of the four atomics writes a genuine base64 value, and a precision rule that correctly fires zero times is the point. ⚠️ RULES 100260/100261/100262 CANNOT FIRE IN THIS PHASE and that is the finding, not a defect. They key on Sysmon EID 13, and Sysmon's own config filters which registry keys emit EID 13 at all. Measured: 400 EID 13 events in a sample, 81 of them Run-key writes, ZERO for HKCU\Software\Policies\...\PowerShell\ModuleLogging and ZERO for Internet Settings\ZoneMap. The endpoint runs SwiftOnSecurity's config, whose registry include-list watches Defender exclusions, UAC tampering, Security Center and Policies\Explorer\Run - but NOT the PowerShell logging policy key, which is exactly what an adversary modifies to blind script block and module logging.

Verified: it matches any 'reg add ... /d <anything>', including 'add x /d ' with nothing following. It fired 30 attack / 15 benign in baseline - exactly one per reg add issued (6 per attack run, 3 per benign run) - while asserting T1027 Obfuscated Files, false in all 45 cases. 100263 restores a real base64 test (>=16 chars) and keeps T1027 where it is true; 100264 catches the rest and drops the false T1027, leaving T1112. EXPECT 100263 TO FIRE ZERO TIMES: none of the four atomics writes a genuine base64 value, and a precision rule that correctly fires zero times is the point. ⚠️ RULES 100260/100261/100262 CANNOT FIRE IN THIS PHASE and that is the finding, not a defect. They key on Sysmon EID 13, and Sysmon's own config filters which registry keys emit EID 13 at all. Measured: 400 EID 13 events in a sample, 81 of them Run-key writes, ZERO for HKCU\Software\Policies\...\PowerShell\ModuleLogging and ZERO for Internet Settings\ZoneMap. The endpoint runs SwiftOnSecurity's config, whose registry include-list watches Defender exclusions, UAC tampering, Security Center and Policies\Explorer\Run - but NOT the PowerShell logging policy key, which is exactly what an adversary modifies to blind script block and module logging.

T1112 CUSTOM-SENSOR phase - custom rules AND a widened Sysmon config. This phase isolates what the SENSOR change unlocks, and exists because T1112 is the first technique in the study whose gap CANNOT be closed by a rule. THE THREE PHASES DECOMPOSE THE REMEDIATION: baseline = default rules + default sensor; custom = custom rules + default sensor (rule fix alone); custom-sensor = custom rules + widened sensor. Without the third phase, 'sensor configuration is the binding constraint, not rule quality' would be an assertion. With it, it is a measurement. SENSOR DELTA IS MINIMAL AND AUDITED: exactly 9 lines added to C:\Sysmon\sysmonconfig.xml, ZERO removed, diffed line by line before applying. Two TargetObject include entries only - 'contains Policies\Microsoft\Windows\PowerShell\' and 'contains Internet Settings\ZoneMap\' - chosen because they are the two paths the selected atomics touch. Widening the config generally would have made this phase measure 'we improved Sysmon' rather than 'these specific keys became visible', and the decomposition would be worthless. Original preserved at sysmonconfig.xml.bak and the modified file is committed as data/sysmonconfig_t1112.xml. GATE CHECKED BEFORE RUNNING, TWICE: (1) EID 13 for ModuleLogging went 0 -> 1 after the config load, proving the sensor now emits; (2) rule 100260 fired at LEVEL 12 on Blue, proving sensor -> agent -> manager -> rule works end to end AND that the DWORD zero-test correctly selected the disable-direction rule over the catch-all 100261. Neither gate was assumed. SAME 150-210s GAPS as the custom phase, deliberately. A phase run at shorter gaps captures more of its own late alerts, so mixing them would inflate this phase for reasons unrelated to the sensor - which is the one thing this phase exists to measure. ⚠️ FROM THIS POINT THE ENDPOINT CARRIES THE MODIFIED SYSMON CONFIG. The two added paths are registry only and are not touched by any remaining technique (T1218.011, T1070.004, T1003.001, T1560.001, T1105 are process, file, process-access and network based), so no later measurement is affected. Recorded here rather than reverted, because reverting would leave the repo describing a config the endpoint no longer has.

SUPERSEDED - attack phase aborted after run 1 and re-run with a different test set. Atomic 2 (rundll32 vbscript:"\..\mshtml,RunHTMLApplication) never terminates: rundll32 persists as an HTA host and ART killed it at the 120s timeout with exit code -1. This window measured 193 SECONDS against ~10s for windows using tests 9/15/16. Same defect that excluded T1082's test 28 - a hanging atomic inflates the window, and a 193s window with a 120s label buffer sweeps in far more ambient telemetry than its siblings, so its counts are not comparable with anything. Retained rather than deleted: the run is real, and the reason for discarding it is a finding about atomic selection. Note the irony recorded in RULE_ID_REGISTER note 11 - test 2 had just been argued to be the one mechanism with no legitimate benign counterpart, and it was then excluded on purely operational grounds.

T1218.011 BASELINE phase. PREDICTIONS WRITTEN INTO RULE_ID_REGISTER NOTE 11 BEFORE THIS RUN. DEFAULT COVERAGE IS TWO RULES AND ONE IS STRUCTURALLY DEAD ON THIS HOST: 92079 (L10) chains from 92078, which requires currentDirectory=E:\ AND cmd.exe in the command line - an ISO-mount scenario, and 92078 is itself mapped to T1204.002 User Execution, not T1218.011. This endpoint has no E: drive, so the only general-looking rundll32 rule is gated behind a condition that cannot occur. That leaves 92081 (L15), which needs the payload to be .html/.htm/.txt/.png/.jpg/.pdf with the ,#ordinal syntax. TEST SET 9, 15, 16: pcwutl.dll,LaunchApplication; url.dll,FileProtocolHandler; zipfldr.dll,RouteTheCall. Each verified to exit with code 0 before the phase ran. THREE ATOMICS EXCLUDED, EACH FOR A MEASURED REASON, NONE OF THEM A DETECTION RESULT: test 2 (vbscript:/RunHTMLApplication) NEVER TERMINATES - rundll32 persists as an HTA host until ART's 120s timeout kills it, exit -1, and its window measured 193s against ~10s for the others; excluded AFTER a failed first run, and session 20260809-110050-attack-r1 is superseded for that reason. Test 12 downloads calc.dll from GitHub at runtime (environmental failure, not detection failure). Test 13 uses `copy` without /Y and prompts Overwrite? on repeat - the THIRD time that trap has appeared, after T1053.005's task collision and T1547.001's REG ADD without /F. ⚠️ MIRROR ASYMMETRY, RECORDED NOT ENGINEERED AWAY: the mirror uses the same two export-proxy mechanisms as atomics 9 and 15, differing only in target, because those are the forms with genuine administrative counterparts - rundll32 pcwutl.dll,LaunchApplication <exe> is what the Program Compatibility Wizard does, and FileProtocolHandler is how Windows opens files by handler. It does NOT cover zipfldr.dll,RouteTheCall, which has no plausible benign command-line invocation. So a rule keyed on the MECHANISM should fire in both classes; a rule naming zipfldr would be attack-only BY MIRROR SCOPE (the 100241/100251 category), not because the behaviour lacks a benign form (the 100260 category). Those must not be reported the same way. ⚠️ FOUR RUNS LOST TO A DEADLOCK IN THE HARNESS, ROOT CAUSE WORTH KEEPING: the benign phase hung at run 1 four times. Cause was Start-Process -Wait in Invoke-ViaCmd - PowerShell's -Wait waits on a JOB OBJECT, so it blocks until every DESCENDANT exits, not just the process launched. This mirror proxies notepad.exe through rundll32; cmd.exe and rundll32 exit in milliseconds, notepad stays open, and the phase waited on a GUI window. technique_name: Archive Collected Data: Archive via Utility
notes: T1560.001 BASELINE phase. PREDICTIONS WRITTEN INTO RULE_ID_REGISTER NOTE 12 BEFORE THIS RUN. EVERY DEFAULT RULE CLAIMING T1560 DEPENDS ON A LOGGING FEATURE THAT IS SWITCHED OFF: 91825 (Compress-7Zip), 91826 (Copy-Item), 91827 and 91846 (::CreateFromDirectory) all chain from 91802, PowerShell Script Block Logging (EID 4104), and EnableScriptBlockLogging is unset on this endpoint - verified by query during T1112, not assumed. Nothing else in the ruleset maps to T1560. This is the T1112 wall reached by a different route: not a sensor filter, but a WINDOWS LOGGING FEATURE THAT IS OFF BY DEFAULT. And the two connect - T1112's atomic 33 DISABLES PowerShell logging, so an adversary who runs Modify Registry first blinds the only detection Wazuh has for Archive via Utility. A measurable technique-chaining dependency, not a hypothetical one. ⚠️ ONLY 1 OF 12 ATOMICS IS USABLE, and that is a finding about ATT&CK's test set rather than a limitation to apologise for. Tests 1-4 require rar/winrar/winzip/7zip - third-party archivers this endpoint does not have, and installing them mid-study changes the environment being measured. Test 10 targets ESXi. Test 12 copies the ENTIRE AppData tree and zips it, which on a 4 GB endpoint takes minutes and would balloon the window past comparability - same reason T1082's test 28 and T1218.011's test 2 were excluded. That leaves test 11, makecab.exe, the only built-in Windows archiver in the set. On a clean Windows host this technique effectively reduces to makecab and tar, and neither appears anywhere in the default ruleset. PREREQ NOTE: -GetPrereqs failed first time because C:\Temp did not exist, so fsutil had nowhere to write the 10 MB sample. Created the directory and re-ran. MIRROR: makecab.exe on a lab file (mirrors atomic 11 exactly, different paths) plus Compress-Archive through a CHILD powershell.exe. The previous T1560.001 mirror ran Compress-Archive INLINE in the runner's own process, producing no child process and therefore no EID 1 telemetry at all - the same defect as the pre-2026-08-06 mirrors that left rule 92027 attack-only. ⚠️ DECLARED ASYMMETRY: no usable atomic uses Compress-Archive, so a rule keyed on it would be BENIGN-ONLY - the first benign-only artefact in the study. It is included anyway because Compress-Archive is by far the most common way an administrator archives anything on modern Windows, and a mirror that omitted it would be unrepresentative of real administration. Report it as a mirror-scope artefact in the 100241/100251 category, NOT as evidence that archiving is benign. ⚠️ CHECK AT ANALYSIS TIME: attack run 2's window is 62 SECONDS (13:24:32-13:25:34) against ~5s for the other four runs. Twelve times its siblings, so it will have captured more ambient telemetry. Compare its per-window alert count against runs 1/3/4/5 and supersede it if it is an outlier - the T1053.005 precedent superseded a 191s window against a consistent 8s for exactly this reason.

notes: T1560.001 CUSTOM phase. Rules 100330 (L8, built-in archive utilities), 100331 (L8, PowerShell compression read from the EID 1 COMMAND LINE) and 100332 (L12, archiver targeting credential material) deployed first. BASELINE FOR COMPARISON: 10 attack / 16 benign with ZERO T1560.001 attribution. Every default rule claiming T1560 - 91825, 91826, 91827, 91846 - chains from 91802, PowerShell SCRIPT BLOCK LOGGING (EID 4104), unset on this endpoint. What fired instead was 92032 (T1087 + T1059.003) and 92052 in attack; 92032, 92004 and 92027 in benign. Collection read as Execution and Account Discovery. ⚠️ 100331 DELIBERATELY READS win.eventdata.commandLine ON EID 1 rather than scriptBlockText on EID 4104, so it covers the same behaviour as 91826/91846 over a channel the adversary cannot switch off from userland. This matters concretely: T1112's atomic 33 writes EnableScriptBlockLogging=0 and would silence the vendor rules entirely. A measured dependency between two techniques in this test set, and the strongest argument in the study for detecting on process telemetry rather than on an optional logging channel. ⚠️ THREE CLASS BEHAVIOURS PREDICTED BEFORE THIS PHASE RAN: (1) 100330 + 100332 MUST BE SUMMED, not read separately. 100332 (L12) outranks 100330 (L8) and the atomic's input is C:\Temp\sam.hiv, so the ATTACK side matches 100332 while the mirror's makecab on report.txt falls to 100330. technique_name: Indicator Removal on Host: File Deletion
notes: T1070.004 BASELINE phase. Tests 4 (del /f a file via cmd), 7 (Remove-Item -Recurse a folder via PowerShell), 9 (delete a Windows Prefetch file). DEFAULT COVERAGE IS THE SAME LATENT PATTERN AS T1112, AND WORSE. Rule 553 'File deleted.' is Wazuh FIM (syscheck), which watches only the agent's <directories> list: %WINDIR% restricted to regedit.exe/system.ini/win.ini, %WINDIR%\SysNative restricted to a fixed binary list, drivers\etc, and wbem restricted to WMIC.exe. NO USER PATHS ARE MONITORED AT ALL, and the scan runs every 43200s (12 hours). Rule 60117 covers Windows event 1102 (audit log cleared) which is T1070.001, not .004. Rules 80106/80791 are Netscaler and Linux auditd. AND SYSMON EMITS NOTHING: FileDelete is ABSENT from the endpoint's sysmonconfig.xml entirely, so EID 23/26 are never generated. Two independent layers, neither able to see a user-space file deletion. TEST SELECTION AVOIDS A TARGET COLLISION: tests 4 and 5 use the same path (%temp%\deleteme_T1551.004) as a FILE and as a FOLDER respectively, and test 6 deletes the same file test 4 already deleted, so any pairing of 4/5/6 would have a run failing on a consumed target inside a single window. 4 + 7 use distinct paths; 9 targets Prefetch. ⚠️ NEW RUNNER SWITCH -PrereqsEachRun, added for this technique. These atomics DELETE artefacts that only exist because -GetPrereqs created them, so run 1 consumes the target and runs 2-5 would measure a failed deletion. Third variant of the repeat-collision problem after T1053.005's named scheduled tasks and T1547.001's REG ADD without /F, and the first where the artefact is CONSUMED rather than blocked. Prereqs are re-created BEFORE window_start so the file-creation telemetry falls outside the labelled window - the creation is not part of the technique. ⚠️ DECLARED ASYMMETRY: the attack side re-creates targets outside the window, so attack windows contain a deletion and no creation; the mirror must create its own targets inside the window, so benign windows contain both. EID 11 FileCreate for .bat files will therefore be benign-only. A harness artefact of window placement, not a behavioural difference - exclude from separability claims, same treatment as 92070/92071's WMI lineage. ⚠️ Atomic 9 (Prefetch deletion) is NOT mirrored: nobody clears individual prefetch entries by hand, so there is no honest benign counterpart and inventing one would manufacture a false negative. A rule keyed on Prefetch deletion coming out attack-only is a GENUINE discriminator (100260 category), not a mirror-scope artefact (100241 category). MIRROR REWRITTEN: the previous version deleted a .TXT file, which is not in the FileDeleteDetected include list this project adds for the sensor phase - the deletion would have been invisible and the mirror would have looked like a detection gap. Now uses .bat files and covers both the cmd and PowerShell deletion paths.

notes: T1070.004 CUSTOM-SENSOR phase. Rules 100310/100311 (EID 1 command line) and 100312/100313 (EID 26 FileDeleteDetected) deployed, AND the Sysmon config extended with a FileDeleteDetected RuleGroup. BASELINE FOR COMPARISON: 33 attack / 20 benign with ZERO T1070.004 attribution. THREE independent layers each failed to see a file deletion: (a) FIM rule 553 reads syscheck, which watches only %WINDIR% restricted to three filenames, %WINDIR%\SysNative restricted to a fixed binary list, drivers\etc and wbem/WMIC.exe - NO USER PATHS - on a 43200s scan; (b) FileDelete was absent from sysmonconfig.xml entirely so EID 23/26 were never generated; (c) even with the sensor on, base rule 61654 (sysmon_event_26) is LEVEL 0 with NO CHILDREN, so Wazuh emits nothing for a deletion regardless. What fired instead: 92027 (T1059.001) 19/5, 92052 (T1059.003) 8/0, 92004 (T1059.003) 6/5. Defense Evasion read as Execution for the fourth time after T1082, T1016 and T1112. ⚠️ THE HIGHEST-SEVERITY ALERT IN THE BASELINE FIRED ONLY ON BENIGN ACTIVITY: 92213, LEVEL 15, mapped T1105, fired 10 times in benign and ZERO in attack - on the mirror's .bat files being written to Temp. Partly the declared window-placement asymmetry (attack re-creates targets BEFORE the window opens via -PrereqsEachRun, the mirror must create them inside it), but assigning severity 15 to a batch file in a temp directory is a precision defect regardless. Third appearance of 92213 as pure noise after __PSScriptPolicyTest and the Add-Type/csc artefact - 551 alerts dataset-wide from one rule, none a detection. ⚠️ THE SENSOR CHANGE WAS SILENTLY DISCARDED ON THE FIRST ATTEMPT AND THE PROBE IS WHAT CAUGHT IT. sysmonconfig.xml declared schemaversion=4.50; FileDeleteDetected requires 4.60+. Sysmon ACCEPTS a config with an older schema and simply IGNORES elements that schema does not define - it printed 'Configuration file validated' and 'Configuration updated', and emitted no EID 26 at all. Found only because the gate check (create a .bat, delete it, count EID 26) returned zero. Fixed by raising the declared schema to 4.90, which the installed Sysmon 15.21 supports (it reports 4.91). ONE ATTRIBUTE CHANGED. Same failure shape as every other silent defect here: the tool reported success and produced a plausible-looking nothing. It also means 'the config loaded' is never evidence that the config took effect - only a probe for the event itself is. ⚠️ WHY THIS TECHNIQUE MATTERS ALONGSIDE T1003.001: 100310/100311 read the EID 1 COMMAND LINE and work under the DEFAULT sensor with no config change at all. T1003.001 has no such alternative - ProcessAccess is the only possible source. So 'the sensor is the ceiling' is fully true for LSASS access and only HALF true for file deletion, where the sensor change adds file-level confirmation rather than being the difference between blind and sighted. The two should be contrasted directly rather than presented as one finding. ⚠️ PREDICTED CLASS BEHAVIOUR: 100310 and 100312 in BOTH classes (the mirror deletes a .bat via cmd del and a folder via Remove-Item, exactly as the atomics do - deleting files is not adversarial). 100311 and 100313 ATTACK-ONLY and GENUINELY so, not by mirror scope: they key on deletion of forensic artefacts (Prefetch, event logs, USN journal, shadow copies), atomic 9 deletes a Prefetch file, and the mirror deliberately does not because nobody clears individual prefetch entries by hand. Same category as 100260 and 100332. ⚠️ 100311's regex was corrected in the dry-run before deployment: the first draft used wevtutil\s+cl and vssadmin\s+delete\s+shadows, which MISS 'wevtutil.exe cl Security' and 'vssadmin.exe delete shadows' because the .exe and often a closing quote sit between the binary name and its subcommand. Same class of error as rule 100200's missing /del - the pattern was written against how the command is spoken about, not how it appears on a real command line. ⚠️ CHECK PER-WINDOW COUNTS: attack-r1 ran 62s against ~7s for runs 2-5 (Prefetch deletion is slower than a temp-file delete). The equivalent 62s outlier on T1560.001 proved clean - all five windows produced identical counts - so window length alone is not grounds for superseding.
